question: Why is the Royal Box always to one side of the auditorium? It's always on the right-hand side as you face the stage. And why isn't it bang in the middle? Because surely the best view would be right from the very middle of the gallery or something, rather than on the side.
Why is popcorn synonymous with going to the cinema? Where does that come from?
Why do we take our hats off when a hearse goes by? Why the hat, and where did it originate from?

Is there any sort of linguistic or grammatical or underlying reason for the order of names in famous groups or pairs? Like Bonnie and Clyde and Tom and Jerry. Why is it Tom and Jerry? Not Jerry and Tom?

When an organ is playing in a cathedral and you get to the end of whatever they're playing, you've got this huge noise echoing through the cathedral. And then when the organ player stops, it carries on echoing for a millisecond and then it seems to go flat. It's almost like it's not like they've played the last note flat. Is it the echo that goes flat? It's not coming out of the organ. It's resonating around the building. And it's that resonance which drops down a half tone. Why does the echoing organ in a cathedral go flat right at the end?
Why is there a time delay between two televisions both playing LBC? She has the LBC app on both her upstairs and downstairs televisions, and there's always a delay between them.

How can Mark paint his puppet theatres with coach enamel in hot weather without getting bugs landing on the wet paint? When he paints outside early evening when it's cooler, he gets bugs on it. If he paints inside with extraction fans, the theatres are too big to paint inside.
Why in music do we count 'one, two, three, four' and then play on four, but in dance we count 'one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight' and throw on eight?
What is the origin of 'something old, something new, something borrowed, something blue'?
Do dogs have different blood types like humans do?
Why do magpies like shiny things, why do they pick them up and fly away with them?
Why don't people ride zebras? They look like horses and donkeys, part of the same genus, but no one ever rides them.
Do flies get stressed? Do they feel anxiety? What is it that causes them to go faster (fly in circles under lampshades)?
Why do the Irish elm pipes have to be played while sitting down? What was the origin of that? Unlike Scottish Highland pipes which can be played standing or marching.
What is the origin of the phrase 'screaming blue murder'?
Why do bouncers at nightclubs say 'one in, one out' when logically it should be 'one out, one in'? It doesn't make sense chronologically.
Why do different beaches have different granularities of sand? In Cornwall, different beaches within miles had radically different sand - fine powdery vs coarse sharp vs pebbles.
How do World Cup commentating competitors know every name of every player? They can't see the names on the backs of shirts from the box.
When snooker players lean over the table to take shots, they rhythmically raise and lower their middle finger - what are they doing and why?
In the show Legends (set in 1990), there's a kitchen scene with ketchup bottles and other period products. Do production companies make these items themselves or get the manufacturer to produce them?
When a river meets the sea, you can often see a visible line where freshwater meets saltwater. Why does this happen and why doesn't it just homogenise immediately?
Where did the Mexican wave originate and why is it called Mexican?
Why are the metal zips on trousers called 'flies'?
Does the heart of a caterpillar stay in it as it goes through the chrysalis stage to become a butterfly?
Why does Europe have 100, 200, and 500 euro notes but the UK doesn't have equivalent high denomination sterling notes?
Is there a word which is unique in each language - with no relationship to any equivalent word in other languages?
Does a cat's meow have an accent? Will a cat from Manchester sound different from a cat in Spain?
Why are slugs targeting my dishwasher specifically and not other appliances like the toaster or kettle? They've destroyed two dishwashers by getting into the electrics.
Why do they weigh our luggage at the airport but not weigh the passengers? Surely we need to know the weight of passengers for fuel calculation and weight distribution.
Why do I prefer to make tea in only five of our fifteen mugs, with a clear favourite? And why does my wife prefer the same mugs? Is it psychological?
How do scientists know plastic takes 400 to 1000 years to decompose when plastic has only been around for about 80 years? They can't have observed this.
How are cats able to eat an entire mouse while leaving the gallbladder completely intact? They don't touch it at all.
How does my new smartwatch know when I'm standing up versus sitting down? My hand position changes very little between sitting and standing.
How many unique jokes are there on Penguin bar packets? I count six or eight so far but get repeats.

The temperature outside is 16 degrees centigrade and warm, but my office air conditioning is set to 16 degrees and it's freezing, and my car is set to 16 degrees and it's also freezing. What's going on?
If you're dyslexic, does the language you're reading affect how easy or difficult it is to manage? Is English and the Latin alphabet harder for a dyslexic person than Chinese or Arabic?
Is ticklishness genetic? His daughter who looks like him has extremely tickly feet, the other daughter has no feeling in her feet at all. His father has very tickly feet, his mother has none.
When towns like Southend were made cities during the Queen's Jubilee, would they have to rename their football team?
Why does his nose not run when he sleeps, despite having terrible hay fever that makes it run all day?
When looking at a star directly, it appears less clear than when looking slightly to one side. Why does looking indirectly at a star make it clearer?
Why do we say we're 'scrambling' a fighter jet? We scramble eggs, so why use that verb for jets?
Why do bagels have that hole in the middle where all the filling falls through?
When he yawns while listening to music, the pitch of the music drops slightly (about half a semitone). Why does this happen?
Why do we say '86 the chicken' when we have run out of chicken in hospitality? Where does 86 come from?
Why are magazines dated so far in the future? I subscribed in April and received the June edition. Why can't I get the April edition in April?
When putting clothes you've worn once (but aren't yet dirty enough for washing) back in the wardrobe with the clean clothes, does it materially affect them?
What colour is an artificial testicle? I had an orchidectomy and didn't ask what colour the prosthetic was. I want to know if it's like a glow-in-the-dark LED or something.
When as a human race did we start laughing? What made us laugh for the first time? Was it a tickle?
Why do footballers always raise their arm before taking a corner kick?

At Bexhill seafront near Hastings, when the tide goes out there are 4-5 dinosaur footprints. Why are there only those footprints? My son asked why there's no trail - like it walked in and walked away. Why are these preserved and not the others?
When sweating during exercise, is it better to constantly wipe away sweat to allow more moisture to evaporate and cool you down, or to let the natural process take over?
Why does a microfibre disc cloth seem more effective when wet than when dry? When cleaning surfaces, it seems to absorb more moisture when damp than when bone dry.
When did human beings start laughing? What made us laugh for the first time?
Why do cats like to sit on mats or mat-shaped things, even on uncomfortable surfaces like paper on top of Lego?
Why does luggage checked in at the same time arrive at completely different times on the carousel?
When senior Catholics like Cardinals move to the Vatican, do they have to go through normal immigration procedures or get work visas?
Why is the bottom buttonhole on men's dress shirts always horizontal when all the others are vertical?
If walking along a path with a road on one side and a river on the other, where should her chivalrous husband Kurt stand to protect her?
Why do you never see yourself in mirrors or reflections when dreaming?
How long does it take cobwebs to decompose?
Are there any other types of geese that nest in trees?
Why are TV adverts louder than the programs they interrupt? Is there no technical control at the point of transmission?
What's all that about? Where's that coming from? [Easter eggs, bunnies, chocolate eggs being delivered by bunnies]
What would happen to a fly in zero gravity? If it went up in a space rocket into zero gravity, would it fly or would it float around?

In 1968 Richard Burton filmed Where Eagles Dare and in 1978 he filmed The Wild Geese - 10 years apart. In both movies when he's using the radio he uses the call sign 'Broad Sword to Danny Boy'. Why would he use that call sign in two movies years apart and not even the same era of war films?
In London there are lots of equestrian statues - people mounted on horseback. Some have their feet in stirrups and some don't. Why?
All the banks on the high street have gone. Every high street had two or three banks. What's happened to the bank vaults? Were the vaults always in the basement?

Is there a rise of the off-yellow, pale yellow kind of white daffodil in amongst the yellow daffodils? What determines the colour of the daffodil? Is it the bulb, the amount of water, or sunlight? Has there been an increase in the number of off-white, pale yellow daffodils?
Why does the date of Easter change each year?
Are we born with a fear of heights (wobbly knee feeling) or is it developed? Is it nature or nurture?
How can the Artemis astronauts be going further than any other astronauts have ever gone before when they're going to the moon - which everyone knows we've already visited?
Why Easter falls on different days of the year?
What have bunnies and eggs got to do with Easter given it commemorates the crucifixion and resurrection of Jesus Christ?
What happened to the bank vaults in former banks?
What happened to the bank vaults in former banks?
Are we born with a fear of heights or is it developed?
What determines the colour of a daffodil? Why are there more pale/white daffodils appearing among yellow ones?
Does being left or right-handed influence which shoe you put on first?
Why, when you're in the Wirral, are you referred to as 'on the Wirral' rather than 'in the Wirral'? What is the Wirral?
Why do we call Dutch people 'Dutch' when the country is called the Netherlands or Holland, which sounds nothing like 'Dutch'?
Why are there so many words for a bread roll in the UK? (muffin, barm, cob, bap, batch, stottie, etc.)
What are the small hinged metal doors on some canal bridges in Birmingham (foot-squared, hinged, with a key slot, found on older bridges)?
Who invented the first paper aeroplane, and when? Did someone try to create one that looked like an old-fashioned monoplane?
Why in British Sign Language is the sign for clapping not a mime of clapping, but instead waving hands like 'jazz hands'?
When and why did it become socially unacceptable for women to be hairy?
Why can I cycle for two hours in Texas without getting sunburned, but if I stand outside for 10 minutes mowing the lawn, I get sunburned?
What speed would an airplane need to be going at before it falls out of the sky?
Why can one cat eat wasps and bees without getting stung, but the other cat won't go near them?
What do angling shops do with the maggots they can't sell? Do they just turn into flies?
Is the exercise benefit better than the damage from pollution when walking through town where I can taste the diesel from cars?
Why do I gag when I clean my tongue with my toothbrush some mornings but not others? I do exactly the same thing.
Why do we stop enjoying the sensation of being dizzy as we get older, and when does this happen?
Why does flat, previously carbonated water taste different from tap water even after all the bubbles have gone?
Why does your hair always feel cleaner and squeakier when you use a different shampoo for the first time, and then when you go back to your original shampoo, it feels cleaner and squeakier again?
Why is there no Aldi in Northern Ireland?
How do barnacles get on whales if whales don't stop moving and don't scrape around the ocean floor?
When building tall structures like The Shard, how do they get the cranes down if the counterweighted concrete is still at the top?
What is the difference between a pole and a post? Why do we say lamppost, signpost, but telegraph pole and flagpole?
Why did the letters of the alphabet come to be shaped the way they are? Why is an A like an A and not shaped differently?
Why is the swanny whistle (penny whistle) funny?
What is the difference between a coat and a jacket?
Why do mirrors give differing reflections? At home, Surrey looks slimmer in mirrors, but in Marks and Spencer's mirrors, he looks bigger.
What is the behavior?
Why does hot water from a tap sound different to cold water? It just sounds thicker, deeper.
Why does a brand new empty vinegar bottle smell of vinegar even though it's never had vinegar in it?
How do daffodils get planted in the middle of nowhere, miles from any houses or villages? If I want daffodils in my garden I have to buy and plant bulbs, so they're not spread by seed.
What determines someone's sense of humour? Why do I love Stuart Lee but hate Michael McIntyre? Similarly, why do some people love mature sitcoms while others prefer youthful comedies?
Has birdsong changed over the centuries, or have birds always sung the same way since day one?
Why do strawberries now require the hull to be cut out, whereas when we were younger, the stem/core would just pull straight out easily?
How do they decide where to put post boxes? My small village of under 3,000 people has four post boxes on the main road, all within easy walking distance of each other.
caller: Sam (Great Lees, between Chelmsford and Braintree)

question: Who decides which direction satellites go in orbit when launched? How do they avoid all colliding with each other?

Where are all the W's disappearing to? It used to be that you had to have a www. in front of every website, but one by one they're all disappearing. And I checked my own website and it's gone as well. Why?
From old war films, I think it might just be Nazis but I'm not sure - in men's uniforms, the trousers have these weird kind of wings in their thighs. What are they called and why are they there?
Why when you kick a ball through someone's legs is it called a nutmeg?
Why are there no green mammals? It seems like a reasonably useful thing to be, evolutionary-wise. I just wonder why no green mammals have evolved ever.

My daughter had a hamster. Why does it spend its whole life trying to escape? You give it everything - happiness, joy, you cuddle it, stroke it, cook food. And it's constantly trying to find a way out. It would go round and round, bite the corner of the cage. Why are hamsters always trying to escape?
Threadworms come out at night. How do they know it's night? They're so simple they don't have a clock. How do they know?
What is the purpose of a bubble on a bubble hat?
N/A - update about medieval knights book
Why do they use little twigs of conifers on the ski jump landing area, but blue dye on other Winter Olympic events like big air?
Why don't crisp manufacturers use the same colour scheme for their flavours across all brands?
When they built the canals back in the 1800s, where did they get the water from to fill them?
Why is Russia called Motherland and Germany called Fatherland? When was this decided?
Why is fresh ginger the only ingredient measured in 'thumb-sized' or 'thumbnail-sized' amounts? Why don't recipes give proper measurements like grams?
How do bees communicate distances and locations through the waggle dance? Is it an innate ability they're born with, or is it learned?
Who used to wake up the knocker uppers - the people who used to knock on windows to wake workers up before alarm clocks existed?
How does the second flock of parakeets know what route the first flock has taken, even if it's 15 minutes later? The flocks consistently swoop through the same route between the same two trees.
What happens to the metal after you've been cremated? After a knee replacement with titanium, what happens to that metal?
Why is it that we humans all have different enjoyments of taste? Why don't we all like the same foods? Is there an evolutionary explanation for our variation in tastes?
Do people know that they're going to die? Similar to the famous elephant's graveyard, do people have some kind of awareness that the end is near?
Why 12 people on a jury? Is there a religious or political reason? Why not 10, which would be the obvious number?
What is the actual origin of birthday cards? Is it something Hallmark pushed to sell more cards?
Why do spectacles never blow off in high winds when everything else gets damaged - wagons turning over, roofs blowing off?
Why do certain nouns in languages like French and Spanish have a gender attached to them, when English doesn't? Who decides what gender a new word gets?
Do people decide when they're going to die? (follow-up to Robert's question)
What happens to TV and film props that are thrown into water? Do they go and collect them? Let them sink? Are they made from something that disposes of itself in the water?

How come a cyclone is apparently lower than a gale on the shipping forecast? They list wind speeds from 1 to 12, 12 being the severest, but they say 'becoming cyclonic' which seems to refer to a cyclone - shouldn't that be higher than a gale?
How does a tiny weed manage to push through tarmac on my driveway that was laid only 3-4 years ago? How do these small plants have the strength to break through thick and heavy tarmac?

Why do eggs have a 'display until' date that is earlier than the actual 'use by' date? If eggs go out of date on the 30th, why are they taken off the shelf on the 24th or 25th? Why do eggs have their own rules for display dates when nothing else in the store is treated this way?

Why do electric toothbrushes still require the same two minutes of brushing time as manual toothbrushes? What's the point of an electric toothbrush if you don't get a time saving? What's the actual advantage?

Is a helium canister heavier when it's full or when it's empty? If I put a full canister on scales and then empty it, will it weigh the same or will it be lighter? Is the canister filled with a vacuum?
Why does my strong German accent disappear when I sing, even though I sound very German when I speak? How come the accent goes away when I sing?
Why do humans settle in inhospitable places - like frozen north, deserts - when the world was big and the population was small?
Why isn't the medium wine glass size (175ml) exactly halfway between small (125ml) and large (250ml)? Why isn't it 187.5ml? Why do we have these weird uneven measurements?
Is there an absolute hottest temperature like there is an absolute zero cold? Can something be so hot that it cannot get any hotter?
Why don't deer leave Richmond Park? There are no cattle grids on the gates, so they could just stroll out, but they don't. Why?
Is there a physiological explanation for sensing when a room has a tense atmosphere? His blind grandmother can pick up on tension before anyone says a word.

What's the logic behind when football teams choose not to wear their first choice kit? Sometimes teams wear away kits even when there's no colour clash, and sometimes they don't when there is a clash. Is there a hard and fast rule or do they make it up as they go along?
Why is it incorrect etiquette to have your elbows on the table when dining?
With all the money we now spend on vets - pet clubs, hypoallergenic shampoo, pedicures - do dogs actually live longer than they did 25 years ago? If so, by how much?
Why are the fudge brownie pieces in chocolate fudge brownie ice cream not frozen solid? They're nice and soft and gooey straight from the tub - why don't they freeze like chocolate chips do?
Why do they speak multiple languages in Asian countries? (e.g., China has Cantonese, Mandarin, Fukien; Pakistan has Urdu and Punjabi; Singapore has multiple languages)
When clearing bubbles from a bubble bath with the shower, why does cold water disperse bubbles much quicker than hot water?
How do they count the smallest creatures like beetles, ants, and penguins during the annual zoo stock take?
Has any major composer ever written music that is actually unplayable - too fast or too complicated? Would they have to be able to play it themselves to compose it?
Who decides where bus stops should be placed in the countryside where there are no houses nearby? Why are they placed in random locations?
Why do we clap when we applaud? Where did the tradition of clapping come from? Do all cultures clap?
Why do paddle rackets have a wrist strap when other rackets like tennis, badminton, and squash don't?
Why does the Air Mail sticker have French text 'Par Avion' on it when sending from England? Why not Spanish, Italian, German, or other languages?
How was the exchange rate determined in Renaissance times? How did people exchange currencies when traveling? When did exchange rates become a thing?
How did it come about that outdoor workers wore donkey jackets? Why donkey jackets and not another type of jacket?
Why do washing machines have a window at the front? Dishwashers don't have them and top-loading ones in North America don't either.

Why is Molly, our rescue Border Collie, sprouting white hairs on the stump of her amputated tail? She's about eight years old, and it's only happened in the last year. She has no white hairs anywhere else except her face.

Was there one specific battle where they decided to let commoners fight in place of knights? In the Middle Ages, being a knight was almost an honour to fight in battle. At what point did aristocrats stop leading from the front?
How does a kitten learn its name? I've been saying their names and they never respond - only about a third of the time.
Why do we write the pound sign before the number (£5.50)? Currencies always have the sign first, but units like kilograms, miles, metres come after the number. Why the inconsistency?
Why do we stand on the right side of travelators and walk on the left? Since we drive on the left and overtake on the right, why doesn't the same logic apply to escalators?
Why are eggs sold in sixes and twelves?
Why have humans evolved to enjoy music? Even when we were apes, we may have always liked music.
How do shellfish breed? Do they crawl through the sand and find each other? Do they come out of their shells?
Why is it called 'mess' in the army? Why officer's mess, mess tin, mess kit?
Why does Mo sleep through his wife's alarm but not his own, and vice versa at weekends? They have the same ringtone on separate phones.
Why don't deer camouflage their smell when they can camouflage their appearance so well? Deer are perfectly camouflaged against dead bracken but you can smell them from far away.
Where does the saying 'coming out of your shell' come from? Is it linked to the shellfish question?
Why do men lose hair where they want it (head) but grow hair where they don't want it (ears, nose, shoulders, back, knees, toes) around the same time in life?
How distantly related can you be to someone before you have no genetic link? When does a measurable genetic link to a shared ancestor disappear from DNA?
What is the science behind shushing and white noise soothing babies? Why does it work for some people and not others?
Why was there a rainbow around the moon last night?

Why do different ear piercing holes in the same earlobe react to different metals? Her daughter just had ears pierced with titanium. One of her own middle holes can only have cheap metals while another hole must have silver/gold.
Why did my leg cramps disappear when I started wearing socks in bed?
Can animals be allergic to humans? How would you know if an animal was allergic to you?
How does deja vu work?
Why does the UK still use miles per hour on road signs when we went metric in 1967/1969?
Do cats derive any direct benefit from purring?
Why can nobody ever scratch the right spot when you have an itch on your back?
Where do earthworms go during summer when the ground is dry and hard?
Do animals actually get any enjoyment out of eating raw meat and leaves like we get dopamine from cake?
Are the swans in Skiathos, Greece owned by the British King like UK swans?
When tigers are shaved, why are stripe imprints still embedded on their skin, but zebras and dalmatians don't have this?
Who wins the Mystery Hour board game?
Why do police always press down on a suspect's head when putting them into the back of a police car, even when handcuffs are already on?
When you put your head under water in the bath, you can hear your own heartbeat. If a pregnant woman did the same, could she hear her baby's heartbeat?
Who invented the first suit and tie to make it acceptable? Why have we kept the same style of suits for so long?
When people switch from summer weight duvets to winter weight duvets at home, what do hotels do? Do they change duvets seasonally?
Why do batteries have to go in opposite ends of each other? Why couldn't they all just go in the same direction to make life easier?
Why does leaving the stone in guacamole keep it fresher for longer? How does the science work?
Last week there was a question about what makes someone good at singing. Does the same principle apply to artwork and painting? Why can some people draw well and others can't?
Why do flea bites itch? I understand the mechanism, but what's the evolutionary advantage for the flea of alerting its host to its presence? A silent biter would seem more effective.
Is there actually a last person in line for the succession to the throne? If there's always someone at the end, it goes on forever, so there must be a thousandth person in line.
In bingo, number 10 is 'Downing Street', number 22 is 'Two Little Ducks'. But who's Kelly and what's her eye got to do with number 1?
When and why did people from Newcastle start being referred to as Geordies?
Why do words like mutineer, domineer, engineer, auctioneer and Brexiteer all end in -eer?
Why does nothing else boggle? Why is it only the mind that boggles?
What is the neurological or biological reason why some people can naturally sing in tune and others really, really can't?
Why do there seem to be no serial killers anymore compared to the 60s, 70s, 80s? Is it something to do with forensics and DNA technology meaning they get caught before they have a spate of killings?
Why are all pills and tablets white when a lot of stuff is made from natural plant sources?
When a man ascends to the throne, he gets a queen. When a woman ascends to the throne, her husband doesn't get the title king. Why?
At the very bottom of the ocean, deep down, is the water there thicker or more viscous than the water at the surface because of the pressure of all the water on top?
Why doesn't my smallest pot work on my induction hob when the larger pots do work?
Why do we say 'the River Thames' but Americans say 'the Thames River'? Why do we put the river first and Americans put river second?
Why is our brain cross-wired so that the right side controls the left side of our body and vice versa?
Why does putting the avocado stone in guacamole keep it greener for longer?
Why can we hear my grandson Theo's knuckle cracking from six feet away when cracking other joints like your neck can't be heard from one foot away? Is it harmful like people used to say?
Why do locals in sunny countries like Portugal not wear sunglasses when tourists do? Have they evolved differently - have their eyes adjusted to the brightness?
How does our brain remember that we've forgotten something but not remember what we've forgotten? You know you've forgotten to do something but you can't remember what it is.
Since the Christianization of Britain, why didn't the church change the names of the days of the week from their pagan origins (Tyr, Woden, Thor, Frigg, etc.)?

Why is GMT so lopsided? We have 57 days from the clocks changing to the solstice, but 98 days until we put them forward again. Shouldn't it be equal? Also, why is sunset so early (half past four) in winter despite having less daylight?
caller: Bill from Newport, Isle of Wight

question: If I'm cooking dinner and the potatoes are still hard, should I turn the heat up even though the water is already boiling at 100 degrees C?
Why don't bee colonies have genetic issues from what appears to be extreme inbreeding? The entire colony is siblings and cousins, and they've been doing this for hundreds of thousands of years.
Why do people use the word 'Roger' to mean 'yes' or 'acknowledged' on VHF radio?
Why do mammals have milk teeth? Why don't adult teeth just come through straight away?
Why does it seem like posh people have more speech impediments (can't pronounce Rs properly), and why haven't they fixed it with speech therapy?
Why doesn't a pedestrian crossing button change the traffic lights to red instantly, even when no other traffic lights are linked and stopping has no wider impact on traffic flow?
Why do some people get an aggressive impulse to squeeze or bite cute things, while others don't feel that at all?

Why were all the greatest British guitar players (Peter Green, Brian May, Eric Clapton, Jimmy Page, Jeff Beck) born within 20 miles of each other? Was there something in the water or particularly good teaching?
Does it make any difference whether you pour Guinness in one go or two goes? And if it doesn't make a difference, why do they do it? When did this two-stage pouring start?
Why do helicopter pilots sit on the right-hand side while airline captains sit on the left-hand side?
Why don't we have court jesters anymore? When did they die out? Who was the last one?
Why do we instinctively fold our arms one way (one arm on top, one underneath), and why is it hard or uncomfortable to do it the other way round? Is it linked to handedness or is it learned behavior?
Why is it called 'corpsing' when actors break character and start laughing on stage?

Why do some animals' hair grow continuously and need cutting (like dogs, sheep), while most animals' hair grows to a certain length and stops? Is there a genetic benefit or is it due to domestication?
Are High Court judges exempt from jury service? What if they're working on a years-long fraud case?
Why do young children pick their noses and eat the results? Is there an evolutionary reason?
Why do we get two high tides every day when there's only one moon? I can't understand why the tide goes away from the moon on the far side.
Why do baby clothes labels say UK age 12-18 months but US/Canada age 24 months for the same size vest? Are babies in Canada and US that much smaller?
Does sweeping up fallen leaves from my tree each autumn and putting them in the garden recycling bin damage the tree by depleting it of nutrients or carbon?

When we borrow Italian words, why do we sometimes use plurals rather than singulars? Why does a coffee shop have 'cappuccino' on the drinks board but 'panini' on the food board? Why do we pluralise the plural?
Why do tattoos hurt more on my right side than my left side? My chest, back and ribs all hurt more on the right.
How big could a beard be before a boxer wouldn't be allowed to box? Would it act as a cushion, like WC Fields or Brian Blessed's beard? Tyson Fury occasionally has a beard.
How do all the trees know when to start dropping their acorns and how many to drop? Why is the acorn crop so wildly inconsistent year to year?
If you take a multivitamin, paracetamol, and antihistamine all at the same time, how does your body know where to distribute what? How does it know what goes where and does what?
Why do TV reporters shout questions at politicians getting out of cars (like at Downing Street) when they never get answers? Is that the best they can come up with?
Why does my ridiculously loud snore never wake me up, but my girlfriend's much quieter snore can wake me up?
Where does the pound sign (£) actually come from? It's a fancy L with two lines through it - why that?
How did we originally know which foods were safe to eat? Like who first decided to squeeze a cow's udders and drink what came out?
If you boil an egg and put it back in the fridge, does it last longer than a fresh egg or the same time?
Why do women and girls put their hand over their mouth when surprised, but men and boys don't? I've noticed it on DIY reveal shows.
How can the nutritional value of supermarket milk be so uniform when cows' milk nutritional value changes based on their diet, the season, and pasture conditions? Why does it never change?
Why is it that when you have an abandoned building, trees and things grow out of it over days and weeks, but this never happens when we inhabit a building?

Why can some dogs see what's on phone or TV and register what they're watching, while my dog doesn't register anything? I've tried showing her videos of other dogs, birds, and other films like Lion King but she doesn't react.
Why was it less of a shock going back into the sea after 10 minutes in a sauna than it was going in fresh?

Why do humans still have canine teeth if we don't eat raw meat and bones anymore? We have cutlery now.
Why do private planes and helicopters always have serial numbers that start with the letter N?
Why was the Battle of Bosworth fought at Bosworth Field specifically? Did they plan it or just happen to stumble across each other?
Indonesia has 17,000 islands. What constitutes an island? How big does it have to be? Does it have to be habitable or inhabited?
Why does your bladder relax when you get closer to home, and is there any medical reason for it?
What's so alluring about alliteration? Why does it appeal to the psyche?
Is water ever as hard as concrete? At what height would hitting water be the same as hitting the ground?
When does a boat become a ship? What is the difference between a boat, a ship and a yacht?
Is there a legal limit to how many times one can drive around a roundabout before you become a nuisance or before it becomes an offence?
How much energy or power is used to save an email in one of those data centers? How damaging is email storage to the environment in terms of carbon emissions?
Why do white keys on a piano have a lip or overhang beyond the black keys? What is the purpose of this design?
Why does my hay fever not affect me when I'm asleep, but starts within five minutes of waking up?
What is beagling?
Why do Tory politicians hold their hand in a closed fist with thumb on index finger at a right angle to their body when making points on news shows?
Why is orange the only Smartie colour that has a flavour corresponding to its colour (tastes like orange) while all other colours don't taste of strawberry, lime, lemon etc?
How does a plant know when to stop growing? Garden centre labels say small/medium/large climber for the same plant type - why three different sizes?
When clocks were invented in 1650, why did they only go up to 12 rather than 24 numbers?
Why do Y sperm swim faster than X sperm to reach the egg?
Why is the TB jab the only vaccine that leaves a lasting scar?
Will airships ever replace planes as a form of travel? Is the Airlander the future?
Why is there a 24-hour delay before muscle soreness kicks in after intense exercise like a long bike ride?
Why does the word 'penguin' come from a Welsh word meaning 'white head'? Who named the penguin?
Does anyone else live on Downing Street? If Keir Starmer becomes Prime Minister, can he pop into number 12 for a cup of sugar?
Why does honey not go moldy but my maple syrup went moldy after only two weeks?
Why can I not buy blackberry jam in the supermarket?
Has the bumblebee flying question been answered? Given modern computing and modelling, do we now know how bumblebees fly when we were taught their flight defied aerodynamics?
Why is there no live video feed from an airplane cockpit back to the control tower? For safety reasons, wouldn't it be useful?
How is it possible that a road can be underneath a canal? I was on an aero boat going to Little Venice and passed over the A406.
What is the difference between a violin and a fiddle? I saw a performer use different instruments for classical versus folk music and they sounded different.
When I defrost sealed frozen meat in a zip-lock bag, blood always appears on the plate. How does that happen if the bag is fully sealed?
How can I consciously switch between focusing on what's behind me in a reflection versus what's in front of me through a window? What allows me to do this?
Iceland is covered in green and Greenland is covered in ice. Why are they named the wrong way round?

Why is Earth represented on maps and globes orientated north-up? Why wouldn't it be south-up or east-up? It's all relative, isn't it? We were just floating through space. So who's decided that it's north-up?
Why is it called D-Day? My daughter asked and I don't know.
Why do we associate rabbits with eating carrots? In fictional stories, rabbits are quite like a carrot. But naturally, you don't see rabbits bouncing around in the wild with a bunch of carrots.

Have the Northern and Southern Lights ever met at the equator? There was such a big solar storm last Friday that the Northern Lights came very south, even to Lanzarote. I just wondered if there's ever been an event in history where the Northern and Southern Lights have met at the equator.
What's the origin of a deck of playing cards? Does it not all start with the tarot?

On Sunday, the last day of the Premier League season, Arsenal and Man City can only win. They're both playing at home, 200 miles apart. After the game, the trophy will be presented to the winning team. But where is the trophy during the game? What's the logistics of getting it to the right ground at the right time?

How come a surgeon isn't a doctor? I had an appointment with who I thought was a doctor, but he was actually a surgeon. I asked for doctor and his name and was told it was mister. Why do surgeons go by mister instead of doctor?

In Call the Midwife, when women are in the latter stages of labour, they're told not to push and to pant instead. I don't understand why panting stops your pushing. Even sitting here now, if I pant, it reduces my inclination to push. But why does panting prevent pushing? What medical thing happens in the body?
Why is it that carrots take forever to cook in tomato sauce? If you simmer carrots in water, they're ready in 5-10 minutes, but if you put them in a tomato sauce for a curry, they take forever.
Why is it when you go on an escalator that's not on, you still get the sensation of being pulled, even though it's not moving?

In France they told me white wine winds you up (enerve). In Portugal they say white wine is bad for your joints - knees and hips. Are these rural myths or could the chemical constituents of white wine be so different from red that you'd have different effects?
How do smelling salts work? What is the mechanism by which waving this magical fluid under someone's nose brings them back to consciousness?
How do groins work? Groins with a Y - the rows of plants that run vertically down the beach.

A tulip has come up in the middle of my grass. I understand birds transfer seeds, but I thought tulips come from bulbs. If they can come from seeds, how does that work? I've lived here over six years and never had a tulip there before.

Did the losing team on Pat Sharp's Funhouse ever get to have a go on the Funhouse after the cameras stopped rolling? My mum used to say the producer was her friend and they let the losing team have a play, but I'm almost certain she was just being kind.
Why do cobblers always also do key cutting and engraving? What common thread of skill training marries those three things together?
Why do towels in hotel rooms work so much better at drying me than the towels I have at home?
I cooked turmeric rice and when I sprayed disinfectant into the sink, it turned the rice from bright yellow to bright red. What chemical reaction is happening?
How much hay would hay lorries actually lose over a journey? Would farmers be compensated for that loss?
In the show Shogun, Japanese words like Shogun and Taika have accents over the O and I in the subtitles. Why do we have accents on English words when they're translated from Japanese?
If you were born blind, could you ever experience dizziness and get dizzy?
Why do railway tracks have thousands of stones on either side and in between the sleepers?
When cakes go stale they go hard, but when biscuits go stale they go soft. They've got the same basic ingredients. Why does the same stuff behave differently?
If terminal velocity is around 122 miles per hour, how come an avalanche will drop at over 200 miles per hour? This question was asked in 2015 and never got answered.
Why do we have England, Scotland, and Ireland all with 'land' in the name, but then we have Wales without 'Walesland'?
Wind and snow can last all day or a couple of days, but why does hail only ever last 5-10 minutes and never longer than that?
How do air fresheners actually neutralize odors? Is it just masking the smell or doing something else?
Why do you have to turn a screw clockwise to drive it in? Is there a reason behind that?
How long have we been asking for autographs? Why did that tradition start and who started it?
How do fish know what species they are in order to congregate with other fish of the same species?
Has anybody actually ever died in the House of Commons or House of Lords chamber?
Where did the idea come from that fish guts could play a part in beer production?
Is there a scientific reason why petrol smells so good to many of us when it's toxic?
When all analogue signals are turned off and we only have digital, what will be the nature of real exact time in broadcasts? How live will things be?
What makes things sticky?
Why do they say a company's 'in the black' when they're in profit but 'in the red' when in debt? Why not 'in the green'?

If you order an expensive wine in a posh restaurant that supposedly needs to be decanted two days beforehand, what do they do? Do they ignore the decanting and serve it suboptimally, or keep you waiting for hours?
caller: Jeremy from Bury St. Edmunds (formerly Belsize Park)

question: Why is it that when long hair is tied up into a single piece, it's called a ponytail? Why is it that when it's tied into multiple pieces, it's called pigtail? Why is ponytail singular and pigtails plural?
Do cats retain memories of traumatic events? Does my cat have a form of feline PTSD?
What is the harshest, least vowel-y language in the world?
When Rangers and Celtic play in Glasgow, why is it called the Old Firm Derby?

When the Bank of England increases interest rates and my mortgage payment goes up from £1,000 to £1,500, has the retail bank (Barclays, Bank of Scotland etc.) instantly made a windfall of £500 profit?
How did sail-powered ships travel up the Thames to the docks on calm days when there was no wind?
Is the white wig worn by judges a worldwide thing? Why only in some countries?
Why were Native Americans once known as 'Red Indians'?
Why have pheasants got a death wish? Why are they so stupid and can't get out of the way of cars?
Why can my daughter's brother unlock her iPhone with his face using Face ID? They look similar but she's got blue eyes and long hair, he's got brown eyes and short hair.
What's the texture of the smallest thing in the world? (bracket: I don't know what the smallest thing in the world is)
Why aren't you allowed to drink from the hot tap? My grandad was a plumber and said there's no reason you couldn't.
Why do tins of tuna in spring water, brine and sunflower oil all cost the same? Surely the oil is much more expensive?
If my cat grew bigger than me, would she see me as prey or does she actually love me?

How do they ensure on Mastermind that each person's specialist round questions are equally hard? If one person has Spice Girls and the next has Rhyme and Gods, how do they know the questions are as hard?

Why can't you cancel a button you've pressed on a lift? When your child presses other numbers or you accidentally press 102, you have to stop at every floor until you get to your destination. Why no cancel button?

Why is horse racing measured in furlongs? Every other sport uses yards, metres, every other derivative, but you never hear 'Saka scored a screamer from half a furlong'. Why do we use furlongs only in horse racing?

Do total eclipses happen on other planets in our solar system? It's a bit of a coincidence that the moon is 400 times smaller than the sun and 400 times further away, giving us total eclipses. Does that happen elsewhere?

Where does a fly/gnat go when it gets into your eye? I walked into a swarm, one ended up in my eye. I washed it out with eye wash but never saw the fly come out. Does it enter your body, get pushed out through your nose as a sneeze, or decompose within?
Did gladiators in Roman times have names when they entered the arena? Like the modern TV gladiators who have names like Legend, Fury, Bionic, Electra - did they have stage names?

Why is it that when you're bilingual, you seem to have a different speech or tone of voice between the languages that you speak? In one language you're usually higher, and in the other you're a lot lower. Chris goes higher in Portuguese than in English.

Could you have a light so bright that you could see your entire skeleton? Like when he was a child with a new torch, he could see the bones in his fingers - could you scale that up to see your whole skeleton?

How specific is the training for sniffer dogs? If you take ones that detect drugs, do they only train them for the most obvious stuff rather than obscure drugs like LSD or ketamine? Can the same dogs do drugs AND explosives?
When a high street or residential road is created, how is it decided which end has the low numbers and which end has the high numbers?
Why do we use hand gestures when we speak? Why do we gesture when we're perfectly capable of explaining ourselves verbally?

Is it possible that our devices - Smart TVs, phones, Alexas - are actually listening to us? Had a conversation about halal meats with family and then started getting adverts for halal meats on Facebook, even though nobody searched for anything.
When a person needs a blood transfusion they get blood from a blood bank. If an animal needs a blood transfusion, where do they get the blood from?
All airports in Canada start with a Y (like Toronto being YYZ). Why is it only Canada that does this? Everywhere else you can usually work out the city from the airport code.
How high is the average cloud?
Why do we use the word 'Dutch' in so many different contexts - go Dutch, Dutch auction, Dutch courage, Dutch uncle? What's the origin of these expressions?
Why don't we recall smells from dreams? It's always auditory or mainly visual. Rarely, if ever, is it a smell.
What do you call a female priest? A male priest is a father. What title is a female priest?

Why is arachnophobia commonly regarded as the most common phobia? Why are we largely afraid of spiders and not other very dangerous animals and organisms that we experience, possibly much more dangerous than a spider?

Why do we have two nostrils? We have two eyes for 3D vision, two ears to locate sound, but these two nostrils are so close together that... Do you know what I think? I think what you've done is you've focused entirely upon one function of the nasal passages, as opposed to the other one.

If fruit doesn't taste very good, even though it's ripe and in season, will it have the same nutritional value? I eat fruit every day in the evening. And even if the fruit doesn't taste very good, I will eat it, because I'm thinking that it's doing me good.
Why are roses synonymous with romance? Why is it roses that are typically given for Valentine's Day?
Why do we say 'quid' when talking about pounds? Where did that come from?
When I put watches in storage, if I pull the crown out, does the battery last longer?
Why do you never, ever see baby pigeons?

Why is it that when you're looking at an island across water, on different days it can look closer or further away? I grew up opposite the Isle of May in Fife. And from Murano, Venice looked closer or further away.
Why is it that our moon doesn't have a nice fancy name like all the other moons in the solar system? It's just called the Moon.

My dog can lie under my duvet for hours without coming out for air. But if I go under the duvet, I'll last about two minutes before grasping for oxygen. How can the dog survive under the duvet for that long?

Is it true that an egg can never be fertilized by more than one sperm? The teacher in sex education said the egg hardens after the first sperm penetrates it and no other sperm can get in. But what if two sperm get there at the same time?
Why is bread exempt from having to be wrapped in supermarkets?
My daughter Grace, age 8, would like to know if there's a proven cure for hiccups. She suffers from them at least three times a day.
How do we know with such certainty what the layers of the earth are? We haven't dug all the way down to the middle.
Why is it that when aircraft are coming for landing, they turn all the lights off?
Is there some kind of criteria for the decision making about the colours of football shirts? Why do clubs choose the colours they do?
Why are some people in Belgium called Flemish?
What is it about glass that allows light to travel through it, but for other solid objects light can't?
Where does the suspense music 'dum, dum, dum' originate from?
If a man is 70-80% unwell (has a cold or flu) and his partner is ovulating, would the sperm be less than 70-80% quality? Would a child conceived be only 70-80% healthy?
Why are taxis legally exempt from child seat/safety belt laws for young children? Why can you take a week-old baby in a taxi without a car seat?
When you write a word multiple times, why does it start to look wrong?
Is birds singing at night a new thing? Our cats have started watching TV on a new Samsung OLED.
Why have my two 12-year-old cats started watching TV suddenly? We got a new Samsung OLED TV. They never watched TV before. They watch YouTube cat channels with squirrels.
What's the German word for rucksack?
Why do my fingernails split when I use scissors with my left hand to cut the nails on my right hand, but cut fine when I use scissors with my right hand on my left hand nails?
What's the difference between 'falling over' and 'having a fall'? What are the criteria?
What happens to your stomach when you go over a hump in the road and why doesn't it affect everyone every time?

Why do trees on the roadside of A roads seem to create an arch or space for vehicles without any evidence of pruning? Does a tree feel the movement of air and realize it's a hostile environment to grow into?
Where did my African grey parrot learn to do the wolf whistle and the 'come here' whistle when it was raised as a chick with no humans whistling around it?

Why is it that after 10pm (post-watershed), if a footballer accidentally swore in a post-match interview the interviewer still apologized, but if the same word was used in a drama or comedy show at the same time, it would be acceptable? What's the difference between broadcasting rules in sport versus entertainment?
Before the invention of communication technologies like telephone or telegraph, how did people book holidays abroad? How would they book hotels or transportation?
When do rainy days or windy days become a storm? What is the threshold?
Why was Napoleon known by his first name, whereas most other dictators in history like Hitler and Stalin are known by their second name?
Why do racehorses have such strange names?
How does a dog know which person to go to when two people with identical whistles from the same shop blow them at different ends of a field?
Why does the pitch of tinnitus change when I press different parts of my head with different pressure?
Do the people who do voiceovers in commercials actually speak like that in real life, or do they put on voices for the ads?
Is it ever too cold to snow?
Why can I see clearly underwater when wearing my daughter's non-prescription perspex goggles from the pool foyer, despite having terrible eyesight?
How would our tides change if we had two or three moons like some other planets?
Has there ever been a conspiracy theory that at the time was deemed crazy and derided that actually turned out to be true?
TV continuity announcers - what do they do the rest of the time when they're not announcing between programs?
Why is 'sheep' the same word for singular and plural? Can you think of another animal that's the same?
Is it true that some animals mate for life (penguins, swans, etc.)? Has a species that mates for life ever broken up? Like a penguin leaving a penguin?
Why is it dangerous to put a cold flannel on a child's head when they have a temperature? Her daughter keeps being told by doctors not to do this, and her grandson has had four febrile seizures.
When filling up helium balloons, is the helium canister getting lighter or heavier as it empties?
Why are TV competition PO box numbers always in Derby? Why not London? Has anyone ever won by posting entry?
Why do children start getting afraid of the dark not when they're babies or toddlers but suddenly around school age?
Why do some ancient manuscripts have to be handled with gloves and some don't?
Are the oldest child's genes stronger and do they tend to live longer because parents are younger when they first had children?
Why when we eat pickles does one eye go all squiffy (twitch)?

question: Why are children of school age afraid of the dark? (Additional input to Clare's question)
Why does the sound of water from the tap change as it gets warmer? Hot water sounds softer than cold water.
When you look at a shooting star going across the sky, can you see them if they're coming directly at you?
Is it true that during the French Revolution after they guillotined Louis XVI, they changed the order of playing cards so that aces became bigger than kings?
How do they make synthetic hair extensions? How are they made in the factory without getting tangled up?
When in American history did the American accent that we know today become recognizably American?
What is the significance of Alverchurch in the history of British radio?
What is the answer to the mystery about something that may help stave off Alzheimer's?
What were electric eels called before electricity was discovered?
When cremated people with metal hips, gold teeth, etc., what happens to those metal bits that don't burn?
Why are the numbers on a dartboard in the order that they're in?
If the source of a river is a trickle like a spring, and the mouth is massive, where does all the water come from?
Why does smoke from a bonfire always seem to follow you around, even on a still day?
In America where all denominations are the same size, how do blind people know what they're paying with?
Why does air from pursed lips (like blowing out birthday candles) feel cool, but saying 'ha' with an open mouth feels warm?
When did dogs become known as 'man's best friend'?
Can DNA be transferred from one place to another - like if someone touches something you've touched, can they then carry your DNA to a crime scene?
Why do police always say a dog was 'destroyed' rather than 'killed' when shooting a dog?
When you look on your phone and it gives you the temperature for the day, and next to it it says 'feels like' something else - how do they figure that out? Does somebody go out and stand in the cold?
On a plane, sometimes the flag is printed back to front. Why are the flags printed back to front on a plane sometimes? The Maltese flag was printed back to front with the cross to the other side.
Why aren't there more left-handed people? Why is the population not more 50-50 split between left and right handed?

Old recipes use 'cup' measurements - if it's proportional, why call it a cup? And if cup relates to proportion, what was a 'stick' of butter? Because if a stick is denoting weight, it can't work the same way a cup does.

Humans have an umbilical cord connected to the afterbirth that is cut manually and clamped. What happens to other mammals in the animal kingdom? How do they manage their umbilical cords? They can't clamp them, so what do they do?

Has the gestation period for our species always been the same, or has it changed through evolution? Baby monkeys can grip their mum on day one, but human babies are completely helpless. Were we able to do that when we were monkeys millennia ago?
MRIs are so loud. They go clonk, clonk. Why are MRI scanners so loud? Why hasn't someone come up with a quiet one by now?

Why are albums called albums? The word album means white or albus means white. But an album as a collection of things has nothing to do with the color white. Also, why do stamp collectors collect stamps in a stamp album?
When somebody passes away and they have tattoos, do those tattoos retain their colour? Do they go instantly? Do they not go?
How does glow in the dark work? The emergency exit signs and stars on ceilings - how does that work without batteries?
Why do we in English write I with a capital letter?
Why are there no great white sharks in UK waters? We get dogfish but no great whites, even though there's plenty of food (Selsey is known as Seal Seal Island).
What determines whether a belly button is an innie or an outie?
Why can you see stars when walking in the peaks on a clear night, but when you see photographs of people in space, there are no stars in the background?
What happens when we extract billions of barrels of oil from deep underneath the oceans? Doesn't nature abhor a vacuum? Does this affect sea levels?
When and why did humans first start to shave their facial hair? Early sapiens didn't have big beards, then Jesus had a beard - when did it start?
When you pick up a freshly laid egg from a farm hotel, how do you know whether it's an egg for eating or whether there's a baby chick growing inside?
What is the difference between white noise, brown noise, pink noise, green noise? And is there a black noise?
What is the chemical process that happens when cooking Brussels sprouts, and why does putting a bay leaf in neutralize the pungent smell?
What's the difference between a porter and a stout? Is it how they're brewed or where they're from?
Why are there four blood groups? Why is there not just one blood group? Is it like planets where they're numbered? And when's the fifth one coming?
Why do marine mammals have a horizontal tail fin and fish have a perpendicular tail fin? If evolution was in place, wouldn't they have the same?
Why are so many places in Cornwall named after saints? In Devon there's next to zero.

How do they manage replacing a lost or broken cricket ball? They can't replace it with a new ball - they have to use one that's faced just about the same amount of overs. How do they age cricket balls?
What is the source of the name John Smith being used as an alias? Why is it the default name for an alias?
When we vote, why do we vote in pencil?
Why does tea taste wonderful one moment and then taste like bin juice 10 minutes later when made in the same cup, same kettle, under the same conditions?
Why don't flocks of parakeets bump into each other when they fly over my house close together, very fast and changing direction? Same question applies to murmurations of starlings.
Why do some areas like Bristol use such affectionate terms of address (like 'my love', 'darling')? Is this a geographical or class thing?
As we age, why does our hair go grey, whereas cats' hair (fur) doesn't?
What would happen if your dog was suffering from a really bad headache or migraine? How would the vet test for that since the dog can't discuss its symptoms?
When I watch the sun in the sky, is the sun really there at that moment? Light from the sun takes eight minutes to reach us, so am I seeing the sun's position eight minutes ago?
How much time has to elapse before it becomes acceptable to start digging up dead people from burial grounds or battlefields?
Where does the air inside a bell pepper come from? If it was grown in Morocco, is that Moroccan air inside the pepper, or is it British air from the supermarket?

How were measurements of time and weights measured? When did a second become a second? When was a second invented or worked out? How did they agree upon that measurement and was it the same 500 years ago?
Why does the head at the top of the neck of a violin, cello, or double bass always have the shape of a spiral? Does the shape have a function? Strings wrap around the peg, not the scroll.

Where does the king go to the toilet when he's on a long car journey? If he's driving back from Brighton to London and suddenly needs to go, does he stop at services? Do they have private facilities planned? Is it like bus drivers with a special key?
What dictates how many blades go on a helicopter propeller? I've seen some with two and some with seven or eight.
Is man flu a real thing? Do men suffer from flu more severely than women? Is there a scientific basis behind it?
Can animals see their noses? Humans can see their nose but the brain cancels it out. Does the same apply to all animals - dogs with different nose sizes, penguins with beaks, horses with long faces?
Why do birds stand on one leg? I saw a seagull on a lamppost on a windy day with only one leg visible, felt sorry for it, then it flew off and landed with two legs.
If you mix two different factors of sunscreen - say SPF 20 and SPF 50 - are they diluting each other or adding to each other? Do you end up with SPF 70 or SPF 35?
Why do the numbers on a microwave or LCD clock jiggle and bounce around outside their frame when brushing teeth with an electric toothbrush, but nothing else appears to jiggle?
Why do they still do the scores on paper with two people writing scores on either side of the dartboard when there's electronic digital readouts? What is the history of this and why does it persist?

If a UK passport holder goes to Europe and overstays their 90 days, what is the penalty? If they get stopped by police or on their passport, or if they come back after overstaying 90 days to the UK, what's the penalty?
Why are the majority of fruits round or at least globular?
Why do blind people's eyes move when they're reading Braille?
Who named people black or white? Why are the majority of Africans or Caribbean called black? When did we start referring to ourselves as black and white people?
If in the past I dated Kate Middleton or Diana Spencer before they met their royal husbands, what's stopping me writing a tell-all book about my time with them?

If you have a choir of 10 people and they're all singing, if one sings out of tune it's immediately obvious. If you have 1,000 or 10,000 people in a crowd singing, at least 10% are probably singing out of key but you cannot hear them. What's the cut-off point? Is there a magic number whereby if you have more than this number, you can no longer hear the out-of-tune singers?

Why are certain viruses like chickenpox causing significantly milder symptoms in children than they do in adults if you contract them as an adult? There are others like hand, foot and mouth. Mumps was much more dangerous to contract as a boy because it could affect fertility. So maybe it's got something to do with puberty but why are some viruses much more unpleasant for adults?
When we think of the first rainbow, why does it arc? Why is it a bow?

Why isn't there an abundance of Welsh specific surnames? Scots have Mac names, Irish have O names, but I'm not aware of Welsh Christian names. Jones is just son of John, Williams, Evans, but nothing distinctively Welsh in the way the others are?

Are we witnessing a miracle every single day with the moon? The moon never changes, it only presents one side of itself. It's exactly the right size to cause the solar eclipse effect. The fact that we only see one side of the moon doesn't that strike you as being a bit weird? Is it a miracle?
Why is it whenever I, no matter how neatly I fold away and put away my cables in a drawer, whenever I open the drawer, they come out all tangled up?
How did the graffiti artist get that graffiti onto the motorway bridge?
Why do some people stick their little fingers out when they're drinking?
Why does water spontaneously turn into water vapor? Why does water, all on its own, turn into water vapor, which is still a liquid but floats away?
Why is my chewing gum dissolving after eating chocolate?
Why don't bottles of scotch or brandy have flammable warning diamonds on them like other hazardous products under the sink?
Why are tins cylinders rather than squares? Wouldn't you get more in a box if they were square?
Could there become a point where we add too much weight to a country like the UK, or a continent, or the globe, where the ground breaks or sinks?
Is empathy inherited or developed through experiences?
Why have dogs got jagged lips? Like when you pull down the outside of their mouth, inside they've got a jagged lip that goes round, like really teeny shark teeth.
Why is it that some foods when you eat them affect your mouth, like spicy food and curries, yet other foods like wasabi affect your nose?
If someone has a higher pain threshold than me, are they feeling the same amount of pain but better at processing it, or are they actually feeling less pain than me?

Why is it that when someone says something that can produce a smell, when I breathe in through my nose, I can smell that thing just for one breath? Like if someone says 'do we want onion in the pasta' I can smell onion in that next breath. Or if someone says 'those hot dogs were delicious' I get a whiff of hot dog.

Black hair dye sticks to my ears, forehead, and back of neck for about 24 hours, but on my scalp it doesn't stick at all. I have patches of alopecia so I can see my scalp easily. Why does dye affect some parts of our skin and not others?
How did cartographers map out the world before the invention of satellites, hot air balloons or airplanes?
Why are some places translated? Napoli is Napoli but we call it Naples. London is called Londres in French. Why isn't it just stayed the same?
How many combinations are there for a Yale lock key? Is there a finite number, and could there be duplicate keys? What are the odds that two randomly selected Yale keys would open the same lock?
